proofs.proof_tex:
Fix an outcome of the data in \(\mathcal B_n\), and abbreviate \(r_{H,n}\) by \(r_0\).  By Definition \(\mathrm{def:simultaneous\text{-}band}\), for every \(p\in\mathcal A\) and \(u\in\Omega\),
\[
 \lVert\widetilde H_p(u)-H_p(u)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le r_0.
 \tag{1}
\]
Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:hessian\text{-}ellipticity}\) states that \(H_p(u)\succeq mI_d\).  Hence, for every unit vector \(x\in\mathbb R^d\), equation (1) gives
\[
 x^{\mathsf T}\widetilde H_p(u)x
 \ge x^{\mathsf T}H_p(u)x-r_0
 \ge m-r_0
 \ge \frac m2>\frac m4.
 \tag{2}
\]
The field \(\widetilde H_p\) is symmetric by Definition \(\mathrm{def:regularized\text{-}hessian\text{-}estimator}\).  Equation (2) therefore places every one of its eigenvalues strictly above the clipping threshold \(m/4\).  By the definition of \(\Pi_{m/4}\), clipping is inactive and
\[
 \widehat H_p(u)=\widetilde H_p(u),
 \qquad
 \lVert\widehat H_p-H_p\rVert_\infty\le r_0,
 \qquad
 \widehat H_p(u)\succeq\frac m2I_d.
 \tag{3}
\]
The last inequality in (3) and \(H_p(u)\succeq mI_d\) imply
\[
 \lVert\widehat H_p(u)^{-1}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le\frac2m,
 \qquad
 \lVert H_p(u)^{-1}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le\frac1m.
 \tag{4}
\]

Fix \(p\ne q\).  Add and subtract \(H_q\widehat H_p^{-1}\), and use the exact inverse identity
\[
 \widehat H_p^{-1}-H_p^{-1}
 =\widehat H_p^{-1}(H_p-\widehat H_p)H_p^{-1}.
 \tag{5}
\]
Submultiplicativity of the operator norm, equations (3)--(5), and the upper bound \(\lVert H_q(u)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le M\) from \(\mathrm{ass:hessian\text{-}ellipticity}\) yield, pointwise in \(u\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \lVert\widehat H_q\widehat H_p^{-1}-H_qH_p^{-1}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
 &\le
 \lVert\widehat H_q-H_q\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
 \lVert\widehat H_p^{-1}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\\
 &\quad+
 \lVert H_q\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
 \lVert\widehat H_p^{-1}(H_p-\widehat H_p)H_p^{-1}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\\
 &\le
 \left(\frac2m+\frac{2M}{m^2}\right)r_0
 =w_n,
\end{aligned}
 \tag{6}
\]
where the final equality is Definition \(\mathrm{def:simultaneous\text{-}band}\).  Since
\(\lVert\operatorname{sym}(A)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le\lVert A\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\), Definitions \(\mathrm{def:cross\text{-}hessian\text{-}margin}\) and \(\mathrm{def:regularized\text{-}hessian\text{-}estimator}\) turn (6) into
\[
 \sup_{u\in\Omega}
 \lVert\widehat S_{pq}(u)-S_{pq}(u)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le w_n.
 \tag{7}
\]

For completeness, if \(A\) and \(B\) are symmetric, their Rayleigh representations give
\[
 \lambda_{\min}(A)
 =\inf_{\lVert x\rVert_2=1}x^{\mathsf T}Ax
 \le x_B^{\mathsf T}Ax_B
 \le\lambda_{\min}(B)+\lVert A-B\rVert_{\mathrm{op}},
\]
where \(x_B\) is a unit eigenvector for \(\lambda_{\min}(B)\).  Interchanging \(A,B\) proves
\[
 \lvert\lambda_{\min}(A)-\lambda_{\min}(B)\rvert
 \le\lVert A-B\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}.
 \tag{8}
\]
Applying (8) in (7), and then using the elementary inequality
\[
 \left\lvert\inf_{u}a(u)-\inf_{u}b(u)\right\rvert
 \le\sup_u\lvert a(u)-b(u)\rvert,
 \tag{9}
\]
gives
\[
 \lvert\widehat\gamma_{pq}-\gamma_{pq}\rvert\le w_n.
 \tag{10}
\]
The definitions of \(I_{pq,n}\) and \(\widehat\gamma_{pq}\) show from (10) that \(\gamma_{pq}\in I_{pq,n}\).

Finally, if \(\gamma_{pq}\le0\), equation (10) implies \(\widehat\gamma_{pq}\le w_n\), so the strict-threshold definition of \(\Psi_n\) gives \(\Psi_n=0\).  If \(\gamma_{pq}\ge3w_n\), then (10) gives \(\widehat\gamma_{pq}\ge2w_n>w_n\), because \(w_n>0\), and hence \(\Psi_n=1\).  Every conclusion is pointwise on \(\mathcal B_n\); no probability bound for that event was used.

added_lemmas.statement:
Fix \(\delta\in(0,1/4)\).  Suppose the two conclusions posed in \(\mathrm{oeq:global\text{-}endpoint\text{-}response}\) are resolved affirmatively with constants uniform over \(\mathfrak E_s\): for \(0<\varepsilon\le1/2\),
\[
 \lVert D^2\varphi_g-D^2\varphi_f\rVert_\infty
 \le C\varepsilon\{1+\log(C/\varepsilon)\},
 \qquad
 \lVert\varphi_g-\varphi_f-\mathscr L_fe\rVert_{C^2(\Omega)}
 \le C\lVert e\rVert_{C^r(D_p)}^2,
 \tag{A}
\]
with the first inequality interpreted as zero when \(\varepsilon=0\).  Suppose also that the following boundary-adapted implementation estimates hold uniformly over \(\mathbf P\in\mathcal M_s\), all regimes, and all sufficiently large \(n_\ast\), with one finite auxiliary constant \(C_{\mathrm{aux}}\) depending only on \(d,s,R,m,M,b,B,L\), and suppose the constant in Definition \(\mathrm{def:two\text{-}resolution\text{-}envelope}\) satisfies \(C\ge5C_{\mathrm{aux}}\).

First, a mass-preserving biorthogonal boundary-wavelet projector gives an event \(\mathcal G_n\) such that
\[
 \inf_{\mathbf P\in\mathcal M_s}\mathbb P_{\mathbf P}(\mathcal G_n)
 \ge1-\frac\delta2,
 \tag{W1}
\]
and, on \(\mathcal G_n\), simultaneously for every \(p\in\mathcal A\),
\[
 \widehat f_p=\widetilde f_p,
 \qquad
 \lVert\widehat f_p-f_p\rVert_{C^r(D_p)}\le C_{\mathrm{aux}}\eta_n,
 \qquad
 \lVert Q_{k_n}f_p-f_p\rVert_\infty\le C_{\mathrm{aux}}k_n^s,
 \qquad
 \lVert Q_{k_n}f_p-f_p\rVert_{C^r(D_p)}\le C_{\mathrm{aux}}k_n^{s-r}.
 \tag{W2}
\]
Second, with \(B_{h_n}v=D^2(K_{h_n}v)\), a bounded extension and polynomial reproduction give, for every \(v\in C^2(\Omega)\cap H^2(\Omega)\),
\[
 \lVert B_{h_n}\varphi_p-H_p\rVert_\infty\le C_{\mathrm{aux}}h_n^s,
 \quad
 \lVert B_{h_n}v\rVert_\infty\le C_{\mathrm{aux}}\lVert v\rVert_{C^2(\Omega)},
 \quad
 \lVert B_{h_n}v\rVert_\infty\le C_{\mathrm{aux}}h_n^{-d/2}\lVert v\rVert_{H^2(\Omega)},
 \quad
 \lVert\nabla B_{h_n}v\rVert_\infty\le C_{\mathrm{aux}}h_n^{-d/2-1}\lVert v\rVert_{H^2(\Omega)}.
 \tag{K}
\]
Third, on \(\mathcal G_n\), if \(e_p=\widehat f_p-f_p\), the normalized response satisfies
\[
 \widehat\varphi_p-\varphi_p
 =\mathscr L_{f_p}e_p+\operatorname{Rem}_{f_p}(e_p),
 \quad
 \lVert\operatorname{Rem}_{f_p}(e_p)\rVert_{C^2(\Omega)}\le C_{\mathrm{aux}}\eta_n^2,
 \quad
 \lVert B_{h_n}\mathscr L_{f_p}(Q_{k_n}f_p-f_p)\rVert_\infty
 \le C_{\mathrm{aux}}k_n^s\{1+\log(1/k_n)\}.
 \tag{R}
\]
Fourth, define the centered influence kernel
\[
 G_{p,h_n,k_n}(u,y)
 =B_{h_n}\mathscr L_{f_p}\!\left[Q_{k_n}(\delta_y-P_p)\right](u).
\]
For all matrix-coordinate indices \(\iota,\jmath\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\), its entries satisfy
\[
 \sup_{u\in\Omega}\mathbb E_{P_p}
   \lvert G_{p,h_n,k_n}(u,Y_{p,i})_{\iota\jmath}\rvert^2\le C_{\mathrm{aux}}h_n^{-d},
 \quad
 \sup_{u,y}\lVert G_{p,h_n,k_n}(u,y)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le C_{\mathrm{aux}}(h_nk_n)^{-d/2},
 \tag{I1}
\]
and
\[
 \sup_{u\ne v,\,y}
 \frac{\lVert G_{p,h_n,k_n}(u,y)-G_{p,h_n,k_n}(v,y)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}}
      {\lVert u-v\rVert_2}
 \le C_{\mathrm{aux}}h_n^{-1}(h_nk_n)^{-d/2}.
 \tag{I2}
\]
The resulting matrix-Bernstein and source-net event \(\mathcal Z_n\) obeys
\[
 \inf_{\mathbf P\in\mathcal M_s}\mathbb P_{\mathbf P}(\mathcal Z_n)
 \ge1-\frac\delta2,
 \tag{I3}
\]
and, on \(\mathcal Z_n\), simultaneously in \(p\),
\[
 \sup_{u\in\Omega}\left\lVert
 \frac1{n_p}\sum_{i=1}^{n_p}G_{p,h_n,k_n}(u,Y_{p,i})
 \right\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le C_{\mathrm{aux}}\left\{
 \sqrt{\frac{\ell_n}{n_\ast h_n^d}}
 +\frac{\ell_n}{n_\ast(h_nk_n)^{d/2}}
 \right\}.
 \tag{I4}
\]
Then the raw Hessian envelope is class-uniform:
\[
 \inf_{\mathbf P\in\mathcal M_s}
 \mathbb P_{\mathbf P}\!\left\{
 \max_{p\in\mathcal A}\lVert\widetilde H_p-H_p\rVert_\infty
 \le\mathfrak R_{H,n}\right\}\ge1-\delta.
 \tag{B1}
\]
At \(h_n=(\ell_n/n_\ast)^{1/(2s+d)}\) and \(k_n=h_n\ell_n^{-2/s}\), there are \(C_1<\infty\) and \(n_0<\infty\), with \(n_0\) allowed to depend on the fixed \(\delta\), such that, for \(n_\ast\ge n_0\),
\[
 \mathfrak R_{H,n}\le r_{H,n}=C_1h_n^s\le\frac m2,
 \qquad
 \inf_{\mathbf P\in\mathcal M_s}\mathbb P_{\mathbf P}(\mathcal B_n)\ge1-\delta.
 \tag{B2}
\]
Consequently, for every ordered pair \(p\ne q\),
\[
 \inf_{\mathbf P\in\mathcal M_s}
 \mathbb P_{\mathbf P}\{\gamma_{pq}\in I_{pq,n}\}\ge1-\delta,
\]
and the declared-pair test has size at most \(\delta\) over \(\gamma_{pq}\le0\) and power at least \(1-\delta\) over \(\gamma_{pq}\ge3w_n\).  The selected upper radius has order
\[
 w_n\asymp
 \left\{\frac{\log(C_0Rn_\ast/\delta)}{n_\ast}\right\}^{s/(2s+d)}.
\]
The premises (A), (W1)--(W2), (K), (R), and (I1)--(I4) are a conditional analytic and stochastic program, not membership assumptions on \(\mathcal M_s\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
On \(\mathcal G_n\), (W2) makes the fallback inactive and gives
\[
 e_p=\widehat f_p-f_p
 =Q_{k_n}(P_{p,n_p}-P_p)+(Q_{k_n}f_p-f_p).
 \tag{1}
\]
Apply \(B_{h_n}\) to the response expansion (R), use linearity of \(\mathscr L_{f_p}\), and recall from Definition \(\mathrm{def:regularized\text{-}hessian\text{-}estimator}\) that \(\widetilde H_p=B_{h_n}\widehat\varphi_p\).  This gives the exact decomposition
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \widetilde H_p-H_p
 &=\{B_{h_n}\varphi_p-H_p\}
 +B_{h_n}\mathscr L_{f_p}(Q_{k_n}f_p-f_p)\\
 &\quad+
 B_{h_n}\mathscr L_{f_p}Q_{k_n}(P_{p,n_p}-P_p)
 +B_{h_n}\operatorname{Rem}_{f_p}(e_p).
\end{aligned}
 \tag{2}
\]
By the definition of \(G_{p,h_n,k_n}\), the third term in (2) equals
\[
 \frac1{n_p}\sum_{i=1}^{n_p}G_{p,h_n,k_n}(\,\cdot\,,Y_{p,i}).
 \tag{3}
\]
The first inequality in (K), the final inequality in (R), (I4), the \(C^2\)-operator bound in (K), and the quadratic remainder bound in (R) therefore imply, on \(\mathcal G_n\cap\mathcal Z_n\),
\[
 \max_{p\in\mathcal A}\lVert\widetilde H_p-H_p\rVert_\infty
 \le 5C_{\mathrm{aux}}\left\{
 h_n^s+k_n^s[1+\log(1/k_n)]
 +\sqrt{\frac{\ell_n}{n_\ast h_n^d}}
 +\frac{\ell_n}{n_\ast(h_nk_n)^{d/2}}
 +\eta_n^2\right\}
 \le\mathfrak R_{H,n},
 \tag{4}
\]
where the final inequality uses \(C\ge5C_{\mathrm{aux}}\) and Definition \(\mathrm{def:two\text{-}resolution\text{-}envelope}\).  For each \(\mathbf P\in\mathcal M_s\), the union bound and (W1), (I3) give
\[
 \mathbb P_{\mathbf P}(\mathcal G_n\cap\mathcal Z_n)
 \ge1-\mathbb P_{\mathbf P}(\mathcal G_n^{\mathsf c})
       -\mathbb P_{\mathbf P}(\mathcal Z_n^{\mathsf c})
 \ge1-\delta.
 \tag{5}
\]
Equations (4)--(5), followed by the infimum over \(\mathbf P\), prove (B1).

It remains to simplify the envelope at the selected resolutions.  The definition of \(h_n\) is equivalent to
\[
 \frac{\ell_n}{n_\ast}=h_n^{2s+d},
 \qquad
 \sqrt{\frac{\ell_n}{n_\ast h_n^d}}=h_n^s.
 \tag{6}
\]
For fixed \(\delta\), fixed finite \(R\), and fixed \(C_0>1\), one has \(\ell_n\asymp\log n_\ast\), \(h_n\to0\), and \(\log(1/k_n)=O(\ell_n)\).  Since \(k_n=h_n\ell_n^{-2/s}\),
\[
 k_n^s\{1+\log(1/k_n)\}
 =h_n^s\ell_n^{-2}\{1+\log(1/k_n)\}
 =O(h_n^s/\ell_n),
 \tag{7}
\]
and
\[
 \frac{\ell_n}{n_\ast(h_nk_n)^{d/2}}
 =h_n^{2s}\ell_n^{d/s}
 =o(h_n^s).
 \tag{8}
\]
Direct substitution into Definition \(\mathrm{def:two\text{-}resolution\text{-}envelope}\) yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \eta_n
 &=h_n^{s-r}\ell_n^{-2(s-r)/s}
 +h_n^{s-r}\ell_n^{(d+2r)/s}
 +h_n^{2s-r}\ell_n^{2(d+r)/s}.
\end{aligned}
 \tag{9}
\]
Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:dimension}\) gives \(d\ge2\), and \(\mathrm{ass:smoothness\text{-}index}\) gives \(s>d/2+3\), hence \(s>4\).  By the definitions \(\alpha=(s-4)/4\) and \(r=2+\alpha=(s+4)/4\),
\[
 s-2r=\frac{s-4}{2}>0.
 \tag{10}
\]
After squaring each summand in (9) and dividing by \(h_n^s\), the first two terms contain the positive power \(h_n^{s-2r}\), and the third contains \(h_n^{3s-2r}\); each is multiplied only by a fixed power of \(\ell_n\).  A positive power of \(h_n\) dominates every fixed power of \(\ell_n\), and cross terms are bounded by sums of squares.  Thus
\[
 \eta_n^2=o(h_n^s).
 \tag{11}
\]
Equations (6)--(11) show that \(\mathfrak R_{H,n}\le C'h_n^s\) eventually for a finite class-dependent \(C'\).  Choose \(C_1\ge C'\).  Since \(h_n^s\to0\), one may then choose \(n_0\), allowed to depend on the fixed \(\delta\), such that
\[
 \mathfrak R_{H,n}\le r_{H,n}=C_1h_n^s\le m/2
 \quad\text{for all }n_\ast\ge n_0.
 \tag{12}
\]
The event in (B1) is contained in \(\mathcal B_n\) by (12) and Definition \(\mathrm{def:simultaneous\text{-}band}\), proving (B2).

Apply \(\mathrm{thm:uniform\text{-}margin\text{-}band}\) on \(\mathcal B_n\).  Its deterministic conclusions give \(\gamma_{pq}\in I_{pq,n}\) for every ordered pair.  They also show that a rejection under \(\gamma_{pq}\le0\), or a failure to reject under \(\gamma_{pq}\ge3w_n\), can occur only on \(\mathcal B_n^{\mathsf c}\).  Equation (B2) therefore proves the asserted coverage, size, and power bounds.  Finally,
\[
 w_n=\left(\frac2m+\frac{2M}{m^2}\right)C_1h_n^s
 =\left(\frac2m+\frac{2M}{m^2}\right)C_1
 \left\{\frac{\log(C_0Rn_\ast/\delta)}{n_\ast}\right\}^{s/(2s+d)},
\]
which proves the displayed selected upper order.
added_lemmas.justification: This conditional corollary isolates the complete analytic and stochastic program needed to turn the deterministic event-to-band theorem into class-uniform coverage and the selected upper rate.
added_lemmas.gap: The endpoint-response question alone does not yield the probability event. The corollary therefore exposes, rather than hides, the additional boundary-wavelet, extension-kernel, linearized-bias, influence-envelope, increment, and concentration premises.
added_lemmas.consumer: The conditional matching-separation proposition and any probability-calibrated use of the margin intervals must consume this corollary, not the deterministic event-to-band theorem alone.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Assume that \(r_{H,n}\le m/2\).  On the explicitly defined event
\(\mathcal B_n\), simultaneously for every \(p\in\mathcal A\),
\[
 \widehat H_p=\widetilde H_p,
 \qquad
 \lVert\widehat H_p-H_p\rVert_\infty\le r_{H,n},
 \qquad
 \lVert\widehat H_p^{-1}\rVert_\infty\le \frac{2}{m}.
\]
For every ordered pair \(p\ne q\),
\[
 \sup_{u\in\Omega}
 \lVert\widehat S_{pq}(u)-S_{pq}(u)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le w_n,
 \qquad
 \lvert\widehat\gamma_{pq}-\gamma_{pq}\rvert\le w_n,
\]
and hence \(\gamma_{pq}\in I_{pq,n}\).  For the declared ordered pair, the test obeys the deterministic implications
\[
 \gamma_{pq}\le0\Longrightarrow\Psi_n=0,
 \qquad
 \gamma_{pq}\ge3w_n\Longrightarrow\Psi_n=1
\]
on \(\mathcal B_n\).  This theorem is event-to-band: it makes no assertion about \(\mathbb P_{\mathbf P}(\mathcal B_n)\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The current claim infers a class-uniform raw-Hessian probability bound from an affirmative endpoint-response answer, but the frozen core contains none of the boundary-wavelet, smoothing-kernel, influence-envelope, increment, or concentration estimates needed for that inference. The strongest unconditional result is the exact deterministic implication from the explicitly defined raw-Hessian event to clipping inactivity, product stability, margin coverage, and test decisions.

proposed.justification: The deterministic event-to-margin theorem proves exactly what the raw-Hessian event certifies: clipping inactivity, inverse-product stability, simultaneous margin coverage, and correct separated test decisions.
proposed.gap: Existing sources do not furnish a class-uniform probability bound for the raw-Hessian event on this bounded-domain estimator; that unresolved probability step is deliberately absent from this theorem.
proposed.consumer: Any validated or probabilistic downstream result may use this theorem only after separately establishing that the raw-Hessian event occurs and that its radius is at most \(m/2\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: Remove the unresolved OEQ and sampling dependencies from the deterministic theorem and align its metadata with the narrowed event-to-band claim.

proposed.citation: Hongjie Dong, Jihoon Lee, and Seick Kim. On conormal and oblique derivative problems for elliptic equations with Dini mean oscillation coefficients. Indiana University Mathematics Journal 69(6), 1815--1853, 2020. DOI 10.1512/iumj.2020.69.8028.

prose_updates.tldr: Separate Brenier structure does not guarantee that a same-unit counterfactual composition preserves Euclidean ranks. The exact population frontiers and the robust counterexample to the published Euclidean implication are unconditional, as is the fixed-support Le Cam lower separation rate. The reported Hessians remain everywhere defined by clipping at \(m/4\); on the explicitly observed raw-Hessian event with \(r_{H,n}\le m/2\), clipping is inactive and the rank-margin interval and separated test decisions are deterministically valid. A class-uniform probability bound for that event, and therefore the upper separation rate \((\log n/n)^{s/(2s+d)}\), remain conditional on the unresolved endpoint-response, wavelet, kernel, influence, and concentration program. The eventual validated chord certificate retains its stronger source-product trigger and is deterministic once the required band event and small-radius conditions hold.

project_justification.gap: Torous, Gunsilius, and Rigollet (2024), Section 3.1, Definition 1 and Theorem 2, identify a nonlinear difference-in-differences counterfactual law under cyclical comonotonicity, but do not give the symmetric-cross-Hessian Euclidean frontier, the Hessian-commutation cyclic-gradient frontier, the global margin, or inference for it. Ribeiro, Santhirasekaram, and Glocker's displayed dynamic-transport assumptions admit the audited open-neighborhood Brenier counterexample even though its symmetric cross-Hessian is indefinite. Existing statistical optimal-transport results provide integrated map risk or pointwise map limits, not a bounded-domain class-uniform raw-Hessian band. In particular, the cited response and elliptic papers do not supply the order-zero Hessian modulus, quadratic remainder, or estimator concentration chain needed for such a band.
project_justification.niche: The delivered field-tier contribution is a graph-native common-rank Brenier counterfactual frontier: exact Euclidean and cyclic structural characterizations, an observable rank margin, a robust published-claim counterexample, an unconditional lower testing frontier, and a deterministic event-to-margin certificate. The class-uniform upper band and matching upper rate are a clearly isolated conditional program rather than an asserted consequence of lower-derivative stability.
project_justification.fill: The symmetric cross-Hessian theorem characterizes Euclidean monotonicity, the commutation theorem characterizes the cyclic-gradient subfamily, and the open-neighborhood matrices separate the full common-rank Brenier class from the stronger commuting subclass and refute the audited Euclidean implication under the displayed dynamic assumptions. The estimator uses a positive density fallback and \(m/4\) spectral clipping on every sample. The event-to-band theorem proves that, whenever \(\max_p\lVert\widetilde H_p-H_p\rVert_\infty\le r_{H,n}\le m/2\), clipping is inactive and all margin and threshold conclusions follow. A separate conditional corollary lists the exact endpoint, wavelet, kernel, response, influence-kernel, and Bernstein-net estimates that would yield probability at least \(1-\delta\) and the selected upper rate. The fixed-support quadratic-bump mixture continues to prove the lower rate unconditionally, and the validated certificate continues to use its distinct stronger source-product trigger.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Project each regime density at \(k_n\), use the strictly positive fallback off the computable regularity event, solve the normalized Monge--Ampere problem, smooth the potential at \(h_n\), form \(\widetilde H_p\), and clip spectrally at \(m/4\) before every inverse and margin statistic. Clipping is provably inactive on any raw-Hessian event satisfying \(r_{H,n}\le m/2\). Establishing that this event has class-uniform probability at least \(1-\delta\) requires the unresolved boundary-wavelet, extension-kernel, response-remainder, influence-envelope, increment, and Bernstein-net estimates; it is not a model assumption.

prose_updates.related_work: De Lara and Ganassali (2025), Section 5.3, leave the cyclically monotone SCM characterization unresolved. Torous, Gunsilius, and Rigollet (2024), Section 3.1, Definition 1 and equation (6), define cyclical comonotonicity and show that it makes the relevant inverse composition cyclically monotone; their Theorem 2 uses that condition to identify a treated counterfactual law in nonlinear difference-in-differences. Their framework does not supply the pointwise symmetric-cross-Hessian Euclidean frontier, the Hessian-commutation cyclic-gradient frontier, the sharp global margin, or margin inference, and the common-rank Brenier framework does not claim their difference-in-differences identification result. Ribeiro, Santhirasekaram, and Glocker (NeurIPS 2025), Theorem 4.12 and Appendix Theorem B.11, assert strict Euclidean monotonicity under their displayed dynamic-transport conditions, but their proof uses a state-dependent weighted inner product; the audited open-neighborhood Brenier pair satisfies those displayed conditions while its Euclidean symmetric cross-Hessian is indefinite. Carlier, Chernozhukov, and Galichon (2016), Theorem 2.1, provide common-reference vector quantiles, not inverse-composition geometry. Hutter and Rigollet (2021) establish integrated map-risk rates. Manole et al. (2024) provide plug-in and boundary-wavelet machinery, and Manole et al. (2023) provide pointwise torus map limits, but neither source proves this bounded-domain simultaneous raw-Hessian band. Caja-Lopez, Delgadino, and Kitagawa (2026), Theorem 1.3, control \(C^{1,\alpha}\) potential error, while Theorem 1.5 gives a \(C^{2,\beta}\)-valued differentiable path and its conormal response; neither gives the class-uniform order-zero Hessian modulus or quantitative quadratic remainder used by the conditional program. Dong, Lee, and Kim (2020), Theorem 1.7, gives \(C^1\) regularity for a divergence-form conormal problem, whereas Theorem 1.10 concerns a different nondivergence oblique problem; neither furnishes the missing Hessian estimate. Ghosal and Sen (2022) study rank maps rather than cross-Hessian margins, and Chen and Fang (2019) motivate caution for ordinary bootstrap claims at degenerate nonsmooth functionals. None of these sources provides the validated source-product interval search, whose sufficient trigger remains distinct from the scalar margin endpoint except in the proved small-radius comparison.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The raw Hessian response is order zero and may accumulate a logarithm, while signed high-order smoothing need not preserve positive definiteness. Spectral clipping at \(m/4\) therefore totalizes the statistic. The proved theorem makes clipping inactive only on the explicitly defined event \(\mathcal B_n\) when \(r_{H,n}\le m/2\); it does not prove that event's probability. The conditional probability program still needs a uniform boundary-wavelet projection, a bounded polynomial-reproducing extension kernel, the endpoint linearization and quadratic remainder, influence-kernel variance and envelope bounds, an increment bound, and matrix-Bernstein/net concentration. The finite certificate additionally uses a source-product allowance \((2M+r_{H,n})r_{H,n}t_{\mathrm{ch}}^2\lVert z\rVert_2^2\), and its trigger is not equivalent to the scalar margin trigger at arbitrary radii. Validated interval arithmetic remains necessary, and the lower bound retains its strict-slack nondegeneracy qualification.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The exact Euclidean and cyclic structural frontiers, the NeurIPS-assumption-aligned open-neighborhood witness, the deterministic event-to-margin theorem, the explicit fixed-support Le Cam lower family, and the small-radius validated-certificate implication are proved components. The boundary-uniform Hessian endpoint modulus, the quantitative quadratic remainder, and the wavelet/kernel/influence concentration chain are open; none is supplied by the cited sources. Accordingly, class-uniform coverage, the upper separation rate, and a matching two-sided testing frontier are conditional on the explicitly listed analytic and stochastic program, whereas the lower separation rate is unconditional. The certificate's source-product trigger is a distinct stronger sufficient condition, with no arbitrary-radius equivalence to the scalar negative-margin endpoint and no termination claim at zero margin. No adaptation, irregular-support, coordinate-invariance, unvalidated-numerics, or empirical-violation claim is made. The scalar and simultaneously diagonal cases still reduce to positive derivative ratios.
